parsed.rationale: The two computed properties `HSBColor.uiColor` (line 53) and `HSBColor.nsColor` (line 63) in `Shared/ColorPalette/Sources/ColorPalette/HSBColor.swift` target fundamentally different platform types: `UIColor` (UIKit/iOS) and `NSColor` (AppKit/macOS). Although their structural Jaccard similarity is 0.71, the divergence is intentional and load-bearing: each property must return a distinct concrete type that is not interchangeable, so no single generic return type or shared implementation body is possible without introducing a platform-conditional type alias that would obscure rather than simplify the code. Collapsing them into a generic function would require a type parameter constrained to an ad-hoc protocol bridging `UIColor` and `NSColor`, which does not exist in the Swift standard library and would add complexity with no real deduplication benefit.
